abstract: A phase-field model accounting for large elasto-plastic deformation is developed to study phase, morphology, and stress evolution in crystalline silicon electrodes during lithium insertion. Lithium concentration and deformation are co-evolved with coupled phase-field and mechanics equations solved by finite elements. The model is compared with a nonlinear concentration-dependent diffusion model and predicts a surface-layer hoop-stress transition from compression to tension that may explain experimentally observed cracking.

lithiated_silicon_phase_mechanics: Studies the amorphous/crystalline phase boundary, stress evolution, plasticity, and cracking during crystalline-silicon lithiation.
phase_field_chemo_mechanics: Couples a phase-field description of two-phase lithiation with finite-strain elasto-plastic mechanics and solves the equations by finite elements.
